title: Upper bound on fibre dimension on a neighbourhood
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $S$ a finite type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be prime and $\mathfrak p$ its inverse image in $R$. Write $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ for their residue fields [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$, the map sending $s\otimes a$ to $\bar s\bar a$. Suppose the dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ at $\mathfrak Q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is the integer $d\ge0$. Then there exists $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that, for every prime $\mathfrak p'\subset R$, if $S_g\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')\ne0$, its spectrum has Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$. Here $S_g$ denotes localization at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].
